::api-operation{method="GET" path="/v1/analytics"}
#docs
Everything a chart needs is on the response and nothing has to be inferred:

- **Units are explicit.** `unit: money` is integer MINOR units in the stated `currency`; `unit: count` is a whole number; `unit: bps` is basis points. Never divide by 100 on a guess.
- **`kind` is echoed.** A `stock` is the value AT the end of each period; a `flow` is the sum ACROSS it. `total_basis` says which rule produced `total` — `value_at_end` or `sum_over_window`.
- **Freshness travels with the data**: `as_of` is when the answer was assembled, `computed_at` is when the OLDEST figure in it was computed.
- **A distinct count or cohort rate over a non-calendar window** (new customers, retention, customer churn over `range=30d` or a custom range) is computed for that exact window — `total_basis: window`, with `total_numerator` / `total_denominator` for a rate — never as a sum of its buckets. Rolling presets are precomputed hourly; a custom range is computed on demand for one business.
- **`coverage` appears when the history is partial.** A period it lists is unknown, not zero. Plotting one as zero is how a partial series becomes a flattering chart.
- **Money is never summed across currencies.** A measure held per currency with more than one currency in the window is refused until you name one; counts are combined, and `currency_basis` says which happened.

Anything coherent but unanswerable — a measure that cannot be cut by that dimension, a grain it does not support, a range with no periods — answers **422 with a sentence naming the fix**.

## Query parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `string` | **yes** | The measure id, as listed by `GET /v1/analytics/measures` — e.g. `mrr`, `mrr_new`, `active_subscriptions`. An unknown id is a 422 naming the discovery endpoint. |
| `grain` | `string` | no | How finely the window is cut into periods, independently of how far back it reaches. Weeks start on the business's `week_start` (default Sunday); quarters and years follow its `fiscal_year_start_month` and are labelled by fiscal year when it is not January ("Q1 FY2027", "FY2027" — named by the year the fiscal year ends in). The first and last period are clipped to the window, so a month in progress ends today rather than at its calendar end. At organization scope the businesses' shared calendar is used, or the default when they differ. |
| `range` | `string` | no | A named window. With `business`, it is cut on that business's local dates. Without it, each business's figures stay on its own local dates and the window ends on the last day EVERY business has reached, so a total never mixes one business's today with another's yesterday; the returned `timezone` is then the organization's, a label. The resolved `start`, `end`, `timezone` and `timezone_source` come back on the response. `this_quarter` and `this_year` run from the start of the current FISCAL quarter/year. Mutually exclusive with `start`/`end`. |
| `start` | `string` | no | First day of an explicit window, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. Requires `end` and excludes `range`. |
| `end` | `string` | no | Last day of an explicit window, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. Requires `start` and excludes `range`. |
| `split` | `string` | no | Cut the measure by one dimension — e.g. `plan`, `plan_at_start`, `country`, `region` (UN M49 groups), `billing_interval`, `signup_cohort` (`YYYY-MM` of first payment), `currency` or `business`, subject to what that measure supports (see `dimensions` on the discovery payload). A missing value is its own `none` row, so slices sum to the total. A dimension the measure does not carry is refused by name rather than answered with an empty breakdown. |
| `split_limit` | `integer` | no | How many split rows to return. The rows come back biggest-first by magnitude with ties broken by key, and everything beyond the limit is folded into one explicit row with `kind: truncated` — so a split can never return unbounded rows. A separate row with `kind: unattributed` carries any part of the population the dimension does not describe, whether or not anything was truncated; read `exhaustive` for whether the rows add back up to `total`. |
| `currency` | `string` | no | ISO 4217 code to state the figures in. Nothing is converted here: this SELECTS the currency the figures were recorded in. Omit it when only one currency is present; a money measure with several is refused until you name one. |
| `compare` | `string` | no | Add the equal-length window immediately before this one, as `compare` on the response: its dates, its total, the absolute change and the change in basis points. Refused on a measure whose `supports_compare` is false. |
| `segment` | `string` | no | A saved customer segment's id (`seg_…`, as `GET /v1/businesses/{biz}/customer_segments` lists it): the measure for that population only, computed from the MRR movement ledger. Membership is the segment as it stands TODAY, applied to all of history. Needs `business`, cannot be combined with `split`, and is accepted only where discovery marks `segmentable`. |
| `shape` | `string` | no | `series` (default) sends every period; `totals` sends the same answer with the periods left out — `series` and each split row's `points` empty, every `total` unchanged. A split then reads as a ranked list, and a measure without one as a single figure. |
| `business` | `string` | no | Answer for ONE business (`biz_…`). A filter, not a different question — omit it and the same measure is answered across every business in the organization, which is also what `split=business` breaks down. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | Always `analytics_result`. One of `analytics_result`. |
| `measure` | `string` | The measure id that was answered. |
| `name` | `string` | The measure's display name. |
| `description` | `string` | One sentence saying what the number means — the same text discovery publishes. |
| `kind` | `string` | `stock` — a value AT the end of each period. `flow` — a sum ACROSS each period. Treating one as the other draws a chart that is wrong and looks fine. One of `stock`, `flow`. |
| `unit` | `string` | `money` is integer MINOR units in `currency`; `count` is a whole number; `bps` is basis points; `ratio` divides `value` by `denominator`. One of `money`, `count`, `ratio`, `bps`. |
| `aggregate` | `string` | How a period's figure was derived from the stored daily rows. One of `sum`, `last`, `ratio`, `none`. |
| `currency` | `string | null` | The ISO 4217 code every money figure here is denominated in. Null when the measure is not currency-scoped or the figures are counts combined across currencies. |
| `currency_basis` | `string` | `per_currency` — one currency, nothing converted and nothing added across currencies. `across_currencies` — counts combined, which is only ever done for non-money units. One of `per_currency`, `across_currencies`. |
| `scope` | `string` | Whether the answer covers one business or every business in the organization. One of `business`, `organization`. |
| `business` | `string | null` | The business the answer is filtered to (`biz_…`), or null for organization-wide. |
| `grain` | `string` | How the window was cut into periods. One of `day`, `week`, `month`, `quarter`, `year`. |
| `range` | `object` | The window as resolved, so a client never has to redo the arithmetic. |
| `as_of` | `string · ISO-8601` | When this answer was assembled. |
| `computed_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the OLDEST figure in the answer was computed — the age to show a reader, not `as_of`. Null when the window contains no stored figures at all. |
| `series` | `array of object` | One point per period, oldest first, with a point for every period asked for. Empty when `shape` is `totals`. |
| `shape` | `string` | The shape asked for, echoed so an empty `series` reads as requested, not as no data. One of `series`, `totals`. |
| `segment` | `object` | Present when a segment was asked for: which one, and that membership is today's. |
| `total` | `integer | null` | The headline figure for the whole window, derived per `total_basis`. |
| `total_basis` | `string` | How `total` was derived: a flow is summed over the window, a stock is its value at the end. Summing a stock inflates it by roughly the number of periods. One of `sum_over_window`, `value_at_end`. |
| `split` | `object` | The breakdown, present only when `split` was asked for. Bounded by construction, and explicit about the two different ways it can fall short of `total`: rows dropped by `split_limit`, and population the dimension does not describe at all. Read `kind` on each row rather than its `key` — a dimension whose own values include one called `other` makes the key alone ambiguous. |
| `compare` | `object` | The previous window, present only when `compare=previous` was asked for. |
| `coverage` | `object` | Present ONLY where the history is partial. Its absence means every period asked for has a computed figure. A listed period is unknown, not zero — do not plot it as zero and do not include it in an average. |
| `freshness` | `object` | How long this answer may be reused, matching the `cache-control` header. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | One measure, self-describing |
| `400` | `measure` was not given |
| `422` | A refusal with a sentence: unknown measure, unsupported dimension or grain, a range with no periods, or money in more than one currency |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/analytics?measure=mrr" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY"
```
